raw.assessment: The incumbent appears useful for routine weeks: unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling, although that subgroup does not establish causality. Overall course-set accuracy was 32/40 and median handling was 17 minutes, below the desired performance. Assignment changes concentrate among affected exports, making requested-week semantics a plausible weakness. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. No observed cross-center rows is reassuring only for the sampled cases; the split-course center was absent. Any bounded change must retain private authorized processing, the documented CSV, concurrent attendance entry, six engineer-days and the hosting allowance. Supplied synthetic observations support hypotheses, not implementation conclusions.

openings.claim: Selecting requested-week courses through current assignments or mutable names may create apparent or actual omissions; stable course identity and week-relevant membership may resolve different portions of the problem.
openings.delta: Distinguish historical membership errors from naming mismatches before choosing a correction.
openings.prediction: With intended course identities fixed, assignment-only changes affect exported membership if temporal selection is responsible; rename-only changes preserve identities but alter coordinator recognition if naming is responsible.
openings.probe: In private staging, vary fabricated assignment changes and renames independently against an agreed weekly course set. Compare exported identities and coordinator judgments, retaining the CSV schema. Include a split-course fixture with distinct centers and attendance entry during export. Estimate any repair before committing the six-day budget.
assumptions: Staging can represent these transitions within existing resources.
Historical assignment data availability is unknown; a repair depending on it remains conditional.

openings.claim: Does active checking or correction dominate coordinator handling, or does replacement-file retrieval consume enough active work to explain the target gap?
openings.delta: Separate active labor from elapsed replacement delay; job duration alone measures neither.
openings.prediction: A retrieval bottleneck yields substantial active request, follow-up and download time; a checking bottleneck yields substantial schedule comparison or spreadsheet correction despite prompt file availability.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions with each consenting coordinator for fabricated routine and changed-course exports. Record active minutes by checking, correcting, requesting, downloading and importing; record waiting separately. Compare the dominant components and disagreements between course references.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate ordinary workflow sufficiently to identify a candidate bottleneck.
Session findings cannot establish success across the next 40 exports.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports; their causal roles remain unproven. Replacement delays exceed execution time. The clean privacy sample excludes a course split, and coordinator checking versus importing effort is unmeasured.

openings.claim: Move course-scope reconstruction into a private, center-and-week-specific export manifest. A coordinator confirms intended course identities once; the exporter uses that manifest rather than reconstructing scope from current instructor assignments. Assignment changes and renames become signals to recheck the affected manifest before generating the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Hybrid parents: explicit scope manifests and change-triggered reconciliation. Their interaction converts disruptive changes into targeted review prompts. The speculative capability is automatic reconstruction of course identity and lineage for any week; it depends on stable identifiers, effective-dated assignment/name/split history, and center ownership checks. A presently testable partial capability uses manually confirmed staging manifests plus scripted change comparisons, with secure regeneration from the confirmed scope.
openings.prediction: If repeated scope reconstruction drives the excess work, manifest-based exports should reduce missing-course corrections and active checking time on changed-assignment and renamed-course tasks; unchanged-course tasks should gain less.
openings.probe: Within six engineer-days and existing hosting, compare incumbent and manifest workflows in two short, counterbalanced sessions with each consenting coordinator, using fabricated participants and changed, renamed, unchanged, and split-course scenarios. Measure confirmation, checking, download, correction, and import time separately; inspect course completeness, CSV compatibility, center isolation, and concurrent attendance entry. Include initial manifest preparation in handling time. Only a subsequent 40-export run can establish the stated operational target.
assumptions: Coordinators can establish intended scope despite conflicting or stale timetables; confirmation does not establish truth by itself.
Failure boundary: absent history, ambiguous splits, or unreliable identities require explicit reconciliation rather than automatic inclusion.
Manifest storage and regeneration can fit existing private infrastructure without blocking attendance entry; this requires verification before deployment.
Participant data stays in the private service and authorized center workspace; manifests supplement the existing CSV schema.

critiques.assumption: An agreed weekly set or confirmed manifest supplies a reliable correctness reference.
critiques.limitation: D1-O6 and unmeasured timetable completeness support an evidence gap, not proven timetable errors. Both proposals acknowledge this but provide no rule for adjudicating disagreement; confirmation could preserve an omission.
critiques.opening: Expose unresolved course identities separately from coordinator approval, and test against a fabricated reference fixed before either workflow runs.
critiques.comparison: Stable identities address naming ambiguity; a manifest records intent. Neither establishes missing historical membership. Automatic lineage reconstruction still lacks verified identifiers and dated split/ownership history.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: give conflicting fabricated schedules to coordinators and inspect whether disagreement remains visible rather than becoming a falsely verified scope.

critiques.assumption: Change-triggered review keeps a confirmed manifest valid until export generation.
critiques.limitation: No supplied observation establishes trigger completeness or behavior when ownership/scope changes after confirmation. Concurrent attendance entry is mandatory, but does not itself prove this race.
critiques.opening: Bind confirmation to a scope revision and revalidate ownership at generation without freezing attendance entry.
critiques.comparison: Manifests alone may become stale; triggers alone request review without defining export scope. Their proposed interaction needs a freshness boundary; a missed trigger must not silently preserve approval.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: script rename, split and ownership changes between confirmation and generation, including a deliberately missed notification.

openings.claim: A revision-bound manifest with explicit unresolved entries may prevent stale or ambiguous scope from silently appearing confirmed.
openings.delta: Extend A1 with approval invalidation and an uncertainty state; keep attendance entry available.
openings.prediction: Relative to A1, fewer stale-scope approvals but potentially more handling. Failure boundary: unreliable revisions or ownership checks; this cannot recover absent history.
openings.probe: Proposed, not performed: implement only fabricated manual manifests and scripted revision checks in private staging; compare with A1, then measure confirmation, exceptions and importing in the available sessions. Retain CSV compatibility and concurrent entry. Operational success still requires the next 40 exports.
openings.fit: conditional on six-day and hosting feasibility; original outcome retained
assumptions: A bounded revision check is feasible; verify before implementation.
Synthetic reference correctness does not establish real timetable authority.
Count all preparation and reconciliation toward handling time.
